svg.text: Architecture: a customised Apache Superset 6.1 talking to a local Qwen model served by Ollama, querying any SQL engine directly or through Trino,
with a Redis cache, an optional Celery worker, a request log with user votes and automated tests
namespace superset-ai · access via kubectl port-forward
Flask blueprint + JavaScript, no frontend fork · no table names in the code
Superset core · REST API (datasets, charts, dashboards) · SQL Lab · cache → Redis · async queries → Celery
engine chosen on the AI page
analysis views with the business rules applied:
SQL, outcome, rows, time, user, vote
read-only user, driver in the image

g.text: 1 The user asks a question in Italian, or describes a dashboard.
2 The extension sends the question, the schema (read with SQLAlchemy's Inspector: comments, sample values, reference periods), the engine's SQL rules and the business rules to Ollama.
3 Qwen answers with structured JSON: the SQL, or a dashboard plan with one query per chart.
4 Each query is checked (single SELECT, engine dialect, joins that multiply rows) and run read-only, directly or through Trino; on error or wrong shape, the model fixes it.
5 The answer comes back with the result and a thumbs up / down vote.
6 The page calls Superset's REST API to create or update dataset, chart and dashboard; every request and vote is logged in ai_registro.

svg.text: Also: Superset keeps chart data, metadata and filters in Redis · with -Asincrono the Celery worker runs SQL Lab queries in the background · prove.ps1 runs the automated tests inside the Superset pod.
